title: Netflix Open-Sources Agentic Workflow for Causal Inference
gist: Netflix open-sourced an actor-critic agentic workflow for Observational Causal Inference that automates repetitive causal-analysis tasks while leaving question-framing and evaluation to humans. To evaluate agents without ground truth it combines process audits with human oversight, and in a retention case study its critic caught issues that cut the naive baseline estimate to a quarter.

insights.claim: Netflix's open-sourced OCI workflow uses an actor-critic loop where the actor agent turns an analysis plan into a spec, fills a templated Jupyter notebook and executes it, and the critic reviews output, rates it not_satisfactory, satisfactory_with_caveats, or fully_satisfactory, and recommends spec changes.
insights.speaker: Anthony Alford
insights.so_what: A concrete actor-critic pattern with human framing shows how to automate specialized analysis while keeping oversight.
insights.locator: The human analyst sets up the process paragraph

insights.claim: Netflix frames OCI analysis as target trial emulation, finding the optimal A/B test for answering a question, and evaluated its workflow on the ACIC competition dataset where it was competitive against benchmark systems.
insights.speaker: Anthony Alford
insights.so_what: Benchmark competitiveness lends credibility that agentic causal inference can match established methods.
insights.locator: OCI analysis is framed as target trial emulation paragraph

insights.claim: Because causal-inference tasks lack ground truth, Netflix's workflow combines process audits with human oversight, publishing plans, specs, plots and notebooks that humans can inspect and re-execute, and open-sourced a standalone version to stimulate research on agentic evaluation without ground truth.
insights.speaker: Netflix
insights.so_what: Process-audit transparency is a transferable answer to the hard problem of validating agents where correct answers are unknown.
insights.quote: how do we evaluate agents’ performance on tasks without ground truth? To meet this challenge, our workflow combines process audits with human oversight.
insights.locator: Using agents for causal inference poses a challenge quote

insights.claim: The frontier of applied AI is better workflows around models rather than only better models, as Netflix makes every step transparent, splits work across a running agent and a critiquing agent, and pairs process audits with human oversight.
insights.speaker: Fabio Piazza
insights.so_what: Reinforces that workflow design, not model capability alone, is where enterprise AI value is captured.
insights.quote: A great reminder that the frontier isn't just better models, it's better workflows around them.

insights.claim: In a retention case study, a Claude baseline chose a simple linear regression, but the oci-agent workflow produced an estimated effect just 25% of the baseline after the critic flagged early-adopter bias and a failed placebo test using built-in playbooks.
insights.speaker: Anthony Alford
insights.so_what: Demonstrates the guided workflow catches errors a naive LLM misses, showing measurable analytical-quality gains.
insights.locator: When the research team used the oci-agent workflow paragraph

insights.claim: OCI is designed not for the agent to spit out answers but to guide correct steps while leaving artifacts experts can verify later, and AI agents are good at lowering the entry barrier for specialized tasks like causal inference.
insights.speaker: Taikai Takeda
insights.so_what: Positions agentic tooling as democratizing expert methods, expanding who can safely run specialized analysis.
insights.quote: AI agents are really good at lowering the entry barrier for specialized tasks, aren't they.
